item.title: Upcoming Events — Tue Sep 8 — French Broad River Brewery
item.description:
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. Just minutes from the Biltmore Estate & Downtown, our taproom is a gathering spot for locals and visitors alike. We regularly host live music and entertainment in our taproom, making French Broad River Brewery a lively hub of local activity. From bluegrass to reggae, there’s always something happening. Check out our Events Page to see what’s coming up next! No brewery experience is complete without great food. That’s why we offer French Broad River Pizza, serving up hot, hand-tossed pizzas made to order. Whether you’re here for a quick slice or a full meal, our pizza perfectly complements our craft beers and the lively atmosphere of our taproom. frenchbroadbrewery.com/pizza
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.description: Introducing The Connect: a weekly community jam at The One Stop curated by Women to the Front on Tuesdays, 8-11pm. We’re thrilled to kick off this new jam on August 4 with Melissa McKinney Friends! Asheville Music Hall The One Stop has a long history of being a place where musicians come together. The Connect is about continuing that spirit while helping create something new. This weekly jam aims to be a welcoming, respectful space where professional musicians, rising artists, and everyone in between can come together to collaborate, connect, and learn from each other. Each week will feature a thoughtfully curated group of musicians who will start the night with a short set and then open the night to a jam. item.title: Ask About Our Featured Listings — Wed Sep 9 — LiveMusicAsheville.com
item.description:
Established in February 2019, LiveMusicAsheville.com now reaches thousands of people every week actively searching for live music in the Asheville area. Roughly 60% of our traffic comes from Google Search as we dominate the top of the results for queries such as “Asheville live music” & “live music Asheville”. Meanwhile our direct traffic is experiencing explosive growth, proving more locals are now using us as their go-to music calendar. Our free listings include just the basics of Who’s Playin’ Where & When. Our Featured Listings really stand out among the dozens of events on the calendar every day. While we update every Wednesday for the following Friday thru Thursday, these Featured Listings are published much sooner and include your picture or poster, a description of the event and the venue, website/ticket links and a Google map. We also share these events on our social media stories to help further promote your show.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville — Sun Sep 27, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Coworking for writers in your area! Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.
For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

item.title: A Halloween Walk at the John C. Campbell Folk School in Brasstown NC — Sat Oct 31, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group The John C. Campbell Folk School is located in Brasstown, Clay County, NC. It has classes in over 50 subjects, including art, craft, dance, music, and nature. (My wife took lap dulcimer lessons there many years ago. A family friend teaches there regularly.) This is the place where John Jacob Niles first performed a song he had collected, "I Wonder as I Wander".
We will gather in the main parking lot of the campus. Our first stop will be at Keith House, where there are restrooms. We will go to the Craft Shop, follow some trails, visit the Herb Garden, see the Eagle Dancer Sculpture, and past a kiln. This is one walk where we will definitely not hesitate to stop and look at various things there are to see. Your camera is a must on this one.
Our route is 5 KM/3.1 miles. Tennis shoes are fine, as there is no significant elevation change. Most will not want walking sticks (although I plan to take one). Bring a protein snack and plenty of water. Wheelcha
